home.metaDescription: Zardonis Jeremie ZITTI, product engineer. I design and ship systems end to end, and keep everything I make as a single numbered archive.
home.statement: I <mark>build</mark> <cycle></cycle>, <mark>decide</mark> where they go, and <mark>imagine</mark> what surrounds them.
home.intro:
Product engineer. I design and ship systems end to end, and what I build has no sector: a company's operations, an election, a cultural product, a learning platform. What interests me sits where a product decision and a technical decision turn out to be the same decision.

Over the past year: a multi-tenant SaaS platform in production for many clients, a civic platform, fourteen reference implementations for people learning to ship, and technical direction of a cultural product.

about.label: Who
about.body:
Based in Cotonou, Benin, working remote on GMT+1. Lead architect on a multi-tenant SaaS platform serving five live client tenants, technical director of a cultural product launching this quarter, and sole builder of Skilluv.

French is my first language, English my working one.

decisions.label: Decisions
decisions.intro: A portfolio lists skills. An archive keeps decisions, because that is where judgment shows, and judgment is the part a stack cannot tell you.

one.title: Take the admin out of the product
one.body: An operations team and a learner have almost nothing in common in what they need to see. Two separate applications, rather than one interface permanently compromised for both.

two.title: Two payment providers, not one
two.body: Stripe and FedaPay together. Serving European and West African clients is not an integration detail, it is an architectural constraint worth accepting early.

three.title: Local-first, because the network is not a given
three.body: A nutrition app that is unusable offline serves nobody in Cotonou. That is not a line on a specification sheet, it is the condition for it being used at all.

four.title: A game engine for what could have been a web page
four.body: The chess coach runs in Unity. The constraint was deliberate: it forced the interface to be spatial rather than a list of moves.

five.title: Write the governance before having contributors
five.body: RFCs, a public changelog and a code of conduct, written before the community existed. A community becomes governable when its decisions stop living in private conversations.

about.intro:
Full-stack engineer building production systems end to end. Architecture, backend, frontend, infrastructure, and the part where it actually ships.

I have a bias for real products over demonstrations, which is why most of what follows is running somewhere with users on it rather than sitting in a repository as a proof of concept.
